docs.purpose: Shows the detail page for one building contractor: their profile information, the permits they have worked on as builder, and any contact details other users have contributed about them.
docs.data_story: It reads 4 tables — `entities`, `permits`, `entity_projects` and `entity_contacts` and writes nothing. Its response shape is **unmeasured** as a pick-by-name whitelist — it passes rows through, spreads a row into a computed object, or assembles the payload dynamically, so there is no single list naming what leaves the server. It is called from 1 place: `web_builder_detail`.
docs.under_126: Becomes a **CONTRACT descriptor** of archetype `QUERY`. It declares its `database.reads[]` with named columns, its response projection as an explicit whitelist, its auth class, its rate bucket and its staleness — and `outputs.writes` is forced to `"none"`. Its `consumers[]` becomes the edge list of the fan-out graph — the join nothing in this estate holds today.

notes: No SPEC LINK header. Uses SELECT * on entities and entity_contacts (whole row, not a whitelist); the response is a plain object literal { builder, permits, contacts } wrapping full rows. Called via a template literal from src/app/builders/[id]/page.tsx. | MEASURED 2026-09-15: DISCLOSURE FINDING (PUBLIC, unauthenticated — src/lib/auth/route-guard.ts:72): TWO SELECT * queries. (1) `SELECT * FROM entities WHERE id = $1` at :24 exposes all 19 entities columns including primary_phone, primary_email, website, linkedin_url, google_place_id, name_normalized. (2) `SELECT * FROM entity_contacts WHERE entity_id = $1` at :52 exposes all 8 columns of the USER-CONTRIBUTED contacts table — contact_type, contact_value (a phone/email, per the column's own name and the comment at :50), source, contributed_by, verified (docs/specs/00-architecture/01_database_schema.md:521-532). `contributed_by` is an attribution field disclosed to anonymous callers, and `contact_value` is unverified user-submitted contact data served with no `verified` filter — the query has no WHERE on verified (:52-55). This is the most severe disclosure of the seven routes I covered. Also disclosed: permit-level commercial data (est_const_cost, description, street_num/name/type, ward) at :39-41. Aliases resolved: `p` = permits (:42), `ep` = entity_projects (:43) — both real tables. No SPEC LINK header — the file starts at the import at :1.
